name: Singapore: NEA Recycle Right (blue recycling bin)
scope: Households in Singapore using the blue recycling bins and chutes. All recyclables (paper, plastic, glass, metal) go into the same blue bin.

bins.name: Blue recycling bin
bins.description: One bin for clean paper, plastic, glass and metal. The bins are blue (Recycle Right guide).

bins.name: General waste
bins.description: Items that cannot be placed in the blue recycling bins.

bins.name: E-waste collection point
bins.description: Batteries, bulbs and electronics. Never in the blue bin.

sources.title: Bloobin's Recycling Guide (Recycling_Guide_v6), Recycle Right
sources.note: Linked from cgs.gov.sg/recycleright/know-your-contaminants/. The summary table (S/N 1 to 66) is the item-by-item list used here.

sources.title: Know Your Contaminants, Recycle Right
sources.note: Page last updated 25 June 2026. Source of the 40% contamination figure.

generalRules.text: Most importantly, is it clean? Rinse and dry before putting it in the blue bin. Dispose of it as waste if it cannot be cleaned. If it does not attract pests, it is clean enough.

gaps.reason: Apart from drink cartons and paper cups, the guide does not cover paper with plastic or foil layers.
The guide does not say whether sachets, pouches or capsules can go in the blue bin.
The guide only covers biodegradable bags (S/N 43), not other biodegradable plastic items.
The guide does not cover this material as packaging.
